The top side AB and the bottom side DC each have arrow markings in the same direction, indicating AB ∥ DC. The left side AD and the right side BC each have one identical tick mark, indicating AD ≅ BC. Angle C is labeled as 101°, and the problem asks for m∠D. Reasoning: Because AB ∥ DC, and the two legs AD and BC are equal, ABCD is an isosceles trapezoid. In an isosceles trapezoid, the two base angles on the same base are equal, therefore ∠D ≅ ∠C. Given ∠C = 101°, so m∠D = 101°.
